conviction_note: A mild lean down with an uncertain bar. Q3 consensus (about $2.35M, chartmill) needs +22% q/q growth. The CEO called Q3 'uncertain' on the Q2 call, the year-ago Q3 fell 9% q/q, and the big new payer policies land late (Sep 16) or after quarter end (Oct 15). Cash will print near $4M against the $8.3M aggregators still carry. The name sold both of its last two real prints (-7.6% and -5.9%) despite triple-digit growth. Against that, coverage momentum gives management a strong Q4 story. The bar has effectively one analyst, so findings are capped small and p_up sits at 42, not lower. abs_move is 8.5 on the name's realised print moves and 89% vol.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $2.35M, EPS -$0.35, per chartmill (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/NRXS/estimates, cited via search snippet; the page returned 403 on fetch). The only cross-check is indirect: stockanalysis FY2026 revenue $8.30M from 1 analyst (S&P Global data updated 2026-09-30, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nrxs/forecast/). Less H1 actual of $3.54M (10-Q), that implies an H2 average of $2.38M a quarter, consistent with $2.35M. EPS estimates disagree (-$0.35 chartmill vs -$0.68 stockalarm). No company guidance; the company gives none. Effectively a one-analyst bar (Craig-Hallum, also the ATM agent), so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 412.84K shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 2.3 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/nrxs, read 2026-11-06), about 3.3% of 12.56M shares outstanding. The 2026-09-30 figure was 372.81K, 1.6 days. Not crowded. The option chain is unusable (ATM legs not two-sided), so there is no skew. Put/call OI is 0.03 on 595 total contracts, i.e. what little open interest exists is calls. Tape: the stock jumped +18.5% on the 2026-10-15 coverage release (6.53 to 7.74 on 1.13M shares) and has since given it all back, to 6.25. 5-day run-up -12.3%, including an unexplained -10.9% on 2026-11-05 (6.86 to 6.11 on 188K shares). A 1.92M-share resale registration (15% of shares outstanding) has been effective since 2026-08-03.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue has to grow about 22% q/q to meet the bar. Q3 2026 consensus is about $2.35M (chartmill), and the 1-analyst FY $8.30M implies about $2.38M a quarter in H2, against Q2's $1.93M. Several things argue against that pace: the CEO called Q3 'uncertain' on the Aug 11 call while saying Q4 should show more sequential growth; Q3 2025 fell 9% q/q ($894K to $811K); and the two large new payer policies were announced 2026-09-16 (18M lives, two weeks before quarter end) and 2026-10-15 (26M lives, after quarter end). Q1 to Q2 growth was +20% q/q ($1.61M to $1.93M) and units were +60% y/y, so meeting the bar is possible, not ruled out. My central read is about $2.1-2.3M, a 2-10% miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-11): revenue $811K missed the ~$1.0M estimate (itiger headline); the stock went 2.56 to 2.41 (-5.9%) on the day. Q2 2026 (2026-08-11 bmo): revenue +116% to $1.93M, which the CEO said 'exceeded expectations'; the stock went 6.87 to 6.35 (-7.6%) on the day (Yahoo daily bars). So the name fell on both a miss and a beat.
findings.source_date: 2026-08-11 (Q2 call summary on the page, read 2026-11-06)
findings.why_not_priced: The bar was last updated 2026-09-30 by the only analyst (Craig-Hallum) and still extrapolates Q2's slope. If the market had priced a softer Q3, the October coverage pop would not have reached 7.9 and the estimate would sit nearer $2.0-2.1M. The stock giving back the pop (7.74 to 6.25) may already be partial pricing of this, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 seasonal dip comes from the company's own Q3 2025 release (https://www.santelog.com/actualites-sante-nasdaq/neuraxis-reports-strong-third-quarter-2025-financial-results-driven-22). The coverage dates come from company releases (https://finviz.com/news/392673/neuraxis-announces-medical-coverage-policy-milestone-expanding-access-to-over-18-million-additional-covered-lives). The 'Q3 uncertain' line rests only on a third-party AI summary of the call, not a transcript. Against it: the 10-Q says 'sales to healthcare customers lack seasonality' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1933567/000149315226036978/form10-q.htm), and Q3 2024 rose q/q ($611K to $667K).

findings.finding: Cash will print far below the $8.3M aggregators carry. The Q2 10-Q's subsequent events say the company paid $3.0M of cash taxes on the July 24 RSU net-share settlement. Management said H2 SG&A and burn would rise from Q2's $1.0M operating burn. So Sep 30 cash is roughly $3.5-4.5M before any ATM sales: about 3 quarters of runway, with an auditor going-concern flag. Remaining capacity on the $11.5M Craig-Hallum ATM is small, at about $3-5M after roughly $7M+ used through June. To the question of what the money buys: sales hiring into newly covered regions, corroborated by the CCO hire (2026-09-29) and policies adding 44M lives in Sep-Oct. That is a funded ramp, not distress. The sign is still slightly negative, because the going concern and thin cash make a raise likely soon after the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q3 2025 cash of $4.4M (2025-11-11), the stock fell 5.9% on the print day, and the company raised $2.8M via ATM and warrants in October 2025. On 2026-04-21 an ATM upsize to $11.5M was filed alongside preliminary Q1 results, and the stock rose +3.16% (baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: Data aggregators still show '$8M liquidity, ~21 months runway' (https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/NRXS/neuraxis-medical-policy-coverage-expansion, updated 2026-10-15), so the retail holder base sees stale cash. The $3.0M tax payment is a one-line subsequent event in the 10-Q, not in the press release. If it were priced, the post-coverage rally would not have carried to $7.9 on 1.1M shares.
findings.independence: The ATM capacity and usage come from the 2026-04-21 424B5 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001933567/000149315226018361/form424b5.htm), a separate document. The H2 burn guidance comes from the Q2 call summary (https://tickerspark.ai/ticker/nrxs, the same page as finding 1, a different statement).

findings.finding: Coverage momentum gives management a strong forward story. A national insurer policy for 18M lives was announced 2026-09-16, a second for 26M lives on 2026-10-15, and the company says its footprint is now over 147M lives against about 120M at the September Lytham conference. Management targets over 200M by end-2027, has hired a new CCO and is 'actively hiring additional sales professionals'. With the CEO already saying Q4 should show more sequential growth, the call will likely frame Q4 strongly, and the stock trades on payer coverage.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-10-15 coverage release moved the stock +18.5% in a day, so this name pays for coverage news when it is new. At the Q2 print the CEO's H2 coverage optimism did not stop a -7.6% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The October policy is public and its pop has been fully reversed (7.74 to 6.25), which says the market is not currently paying for the coverage story. Any upside here depends on new data on the call: covered-lives conversion, October or Q4-to-date ordering accounts, or another policy. That is why it is small.
findings.independence: The company's Sep 16 release (https://finviz.com/news/392673/neuraxis-announces-medical-coverage-policy-milestone-expanding-access-to-over-18-million-additional-covered-lives) and the CCO release (https://finviz.com/news/396306/neuraxis-positions-for-next-phase-of-commercial-growth-with-appointment-of-craig-blanchard-as-chief-commercial-officer). All are company-sourced, so not independent of management.

findings.finding: A resale registration effective 2026-08-03 covers up to 1,923,194 shares (about 15% of the 12.56M outstanding): 849,212 shares held by certain holders, 923,776 underlying RSUs and 150,206 director shares. That is a standing supply overhang that can sell into any post-print strength.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since it went effective, the stock has sold off on both the Q2 print (-7.6%) and after the October pop (-19% from the high). Causation is not established.
findings.why_not_priced: It has been public for three months, so it is largely priced. It is filed because it caps the upside of any good-news reaction in a stock that trades about 160K shares a day.
findings.independence: No open-market insider sales have been filed since (massive.com insider summary, https://massive.com/quote/nrxs). That cuts against the overhang being active.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-08, after Q3 had closed, the CEO (268 shares), the CFO (1,937 shares) and the CRO (328 shares) filed code-P purchases at $4.84, while the stock traded at about $6.77. The below-market price suggests a plan or ESPP purchase rather than a discretionary signal, and the amounts total about $12K.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and tiny, and probably a plan purchase. It carries information only in that insiders who knew roughly how Q3 went did not avoid buying.

outside_window.finding: A follow-on equity raise or ATM draw after the print: the going concern plus about $4M of cash make one likely. A registered direct priced after the 2026-11-09 close would fall outside the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR since 2026-10-14: no 8-K item 2.02 and no preliminary Q3 results (unlike Q1 2026, which was pre-announced 2026-04-21), no new S-3 or 424B5
Cause of the 2026-11-05 -10.9% drop: no company news or filing found (an AAII 'down 5.12%' headline dated ~2026-11-01 had no content)
Job postings: no specific territory-manager listings found; only the company's statement that it is hiring sales staff
Q2 2026 call transcript: not retrieved; only third-party summaries (quartr, tickerspark)
Independent utilisation series for PENFS or IB-Stim (claims, prescriptions): none found

rejected_candidates.candidate: Baseline reaction history (2025-10-23 -8.64%, 2026-04-21 +3.16%) used as the print base rate
rejected_candidates.detail: Those dates are preliminary-results or ATM 8-Ks, not the full prints (Q3 2025 printed 2025-11-11, Q2 2026 on 2026-08-11). The real print days were -5.9% and -7.6% per Yahoo daily bars, and those were used instead.
Folded into the bar statement as a disagreement on EPS. Revenue is the line this name trades on.
Search served it as recent, but the article is dated 2025-05-22, so it is history and not a current financing.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The slight negative lean agrees with the -12% 5-day and -9.8% 20-day tape, so part of it may already be in the price, which is another reason p_up sits at 42 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar has one real estimate source; EPS sources disagree): revenue-miss finding capped from -1.5 to -1.0, and p_up moved from 40 to 42.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): the cash finding was re-signed after asking what the money buys (sales hiring into new coverage, corroborated) and trimmed from -1.0 to -0.8. It stays negative because of the going-concern flag.
Rule 1 (this name sold both recent prints, including a beat): the positive coverage/guidance finding trimmed from +0.8 to +0.6.
Rule 8 (thin coverage): abs_move raised from 8.0 to 8.5.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the 2026-11-05 drop stays unfiled.
